lessons.claim: cases/chain_bend_2d.bending_matrix (κ_θ BᵀB with B the second difference) agrees with HOOMD md.angle.Harmonic(k=κ_θ, t0=π) to within 0.55% in static 3-point bending (n=25, δ=0.136 d: the matrix 4813.94 · HOOMD 4840.21 · the beam 48EI/L³ 4830.66 kT/d²). ★ What had been verified until then was only 'the discrete matrix vs the beam formula' at −0.35%, which was **analytic against analytic**, and whether the matrix is the same physics as HOOMD's angle potential had never once been confirmed. λ_max, τ_fast, dt and K*(ω) were all being derived from the matrix, so it was an unconfirmed foundation in use. A measurement tip: the per-particle force array may not be in tag order because of ParticleSorter, so measuring k = 2U/δ² from the scalar energy makes the ordering problem disappear.
